raw.name: Newspaper - 10 Years of Independent Lamang
raw.transcript: 10 Years of Independent Lamang August 17, 1958 The Southeast Asian nation of Lamang is celebrating ten years of independence. The peaceful transfer of power a decade ago has proven to be a lasting success, reflected in the country’s growing economy and expanding industrial sector. “We are grateful that the world remembers us and has sent warm congratulations on our tenth anniversary of independence. It is always heartening to hear from friends in fellow democratic nations,” said President Bounnhang Sayasone. Lamang now appears well on its way to joining the ranks of Asia’s economic tigers. Here’s hoping their story of progress and stability continues. Lamang Participates in Philippine Military Exercise A small contingent of Lamang military officers has joined a training exercise hosted by the Philippine Armed Forces, aimed at providing exposure to new tactics and strategic approaches. This marks the first joint exercise between the two nations. Given the Philippines’ close alliance with the United States, some observers view this as a possible sign that Lamang may be edging closer to the West. Interview — Brian J. Bronstein, Ph. D. Q: Dr. Bronstein, could you describe the current situation in Lamang? A: Lamang is presently celebrating ten years of independence. It has developed into a relatively stable state, effectively utilizing the industrial infrastructure left behind by the British. The country operates under a democratic system, although there is a slight cause for concern: since independence, it has had only one president, Bounnhang Sayasone. While the Lamang constitution does not prohibit re-election, the lack of leadership turnover raises some questions. Q: Would you consider Lamang an ally of the West? A: I wouldn’t go as far as to call them an ally, but they are certainly not adversaries either. Their position is more comparable to that of India, non-aligned and pragmatic. That said, they don’t appear to have much sympathy for the Soviet bloc, if that’s what you’re asking. Q: How do you view Lamang’s future? A: Quite optimistically, in fact. If their current trajectory continues, I can envision Lamang emerging as a significant economic force in Southeast Asia. Q: Thank you for your time, Dr. Bronstein. A: My pleasure. Letters to the Editor Why are you reporting on some Third-world country bumpkins instead of focusing on normal people? We need more coverage of the Reds here in the U.S., not in some jungle. John D. Dear John, We’re called Worldview News, not Only-USA News. What happens in “some jungle” today often shapes tomorrow’s headlines at home. If you want to understand the bigger picture, you can’t just stay in your backyard and ignore the rest of the map.

raw.name: Newspaper - 50 Years Since Liberation from Japan
raw.transcript: 50 Years Since Liberation from Japan September 16, 1995 Today marks fifty years of freedom from Japanese occupation. In 1941, the Imperial Japanese Army landed on our island, driving out the British. At first, we rejoiced, believing we had been liberated from oppression. But it soon became clear that the Japanese, who claimed to be freeing Asia, had only come to impose their own rule. “I was eight years old when the Japanese arrived. We wanted to believe they had come as liberators, but instead, they seized control and forced us to work even harder for their imperial ambitions. The Lamangese must never again trust any outside power that claims to ‘help.’ If we seek true freedom, we must win it with our own hands.” We wholeheartedly agree with the words of President Raksmei Sayavong. Labor Shortage Resolved The recent shortage of workers has been successfully overcome through government-led re-education programs, which enable citizens to transition into key industries. “I was a high school teacher, but thanks to our government, I now have the opportunity to contribute to our nation’s growth in the construction sector,” said one program participant. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh The Japanese invasion of our island was an unprovoked act of aggression, cloaked in the false language of liberation. It struck a devastating blow to our collective psyche. One of the harshest awakenings in our history. For the first time, we realized that the threat to our freedom did not always come from white colonialists. This time, it came from fellow Asians. The Japanese, proud of having preserved their independence from the West, looked down on us with contempt. They treated our people with cruelty and disdain, as if we were beneath them. Yet despite their brutality, we rose up and drove them back to their islands. And what was our reward? To see the British return, swooping in to steal the fruits of our sacrifice. Do not trust the Japanese. They have not learned their lesson. Their government has yet to acknowledge the full extent of the wrongs committed against our nation. The remnants of their brief but brutal occupation still linger across our land, especially in the eastern reaches of Lamang, near Ban Pa. We must never forget the crimes committed during those dark years. Film Review by Nok Dam — Showgirls Ever since seeing Paul Verhoeven’s sci-fi masterpiece RoboCop in 1987, I knew this director was utterly disillusioned with the so-called “American Dream” and presented a biting political commentary on rampant crime, corruption, and corporate overreach. Now, Verhoeven is back again, and what he once did for violence, he now does with sex. Showgirls is a sleazy, vulgar, and borderline revolting. A film that perfectly embodies the culture that produced it. All the characters are despicable and learn nothing throughout the story. There is no resolution, no absolution, no happy ending. Verhoeven puts a mirror to the face of American society, which immediately cracks and is covered by various bodily fluids. And unlike RoboCop, this time the audiences, faced with their own reflection, aren’t too fond of what they’re seeing... Here’s hoping this unique and brave director keeps doing his part in the edification of the American people. Maybe next time, he could tackle the country’s imperialistic tendencies the same way he portrayed its lust for violence and carnal desires. 9/10 Fun with Girls When is a door not a door? When it’s ajar.

raw.name: Newspaper - Another Monarch Bites the Dust
raw.transcript: Another Monarch Bites the Dust September 9, 2022 Yesterday, Queen Elizabeth II of Great Britain passed away, and around the world, nations that have endured British oppression are celebrating. For far too long, this \"lich\" thrived off the blood and labor of others. Under her reign, millions lived in poverty so that she and her family could enjoy a life of luxury. “The death of Elizabeth II is a positive development for Lamang. Every imperialist who oppressed us deserves to die. The only unfortunate part is that it took this long,” said Vice President Jan Park. We stand firmly with our representatives. Down with the aristocracy! It’s time to follow the French example and send them all to the guillotine. Celebrations Around Lamang Across Lamang, work came to a halt as people poured into the streets to celebrate the death of the British oppressor. “We are thankful that the British are mourning. Long live President Narith Sayavong!” said food vendor Anan Vongphakdy. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh What greater joy could a jungle-born like me feel than at the death of one of history’s greatest oppressors? Elizabeth is gone, and I could not be more elated. While the British may grieve, much of the world breathes a sigh of relief. Justice has finally caught up. Few nations escaped the reach of the British Empire, and scars remain wherever they set foot. Just look at their closest neighbor, Ireland — even they know better than to trust the British. Every nation deserves freedom from the parasites we call aristocracy, pampered elites living off wealth built with blood-stained hands. Thank the heavens we Lamangese are not like them. Film Review by Nok Dam — Medieval Medieval is a historical action drama inspired by the life of Czech national hero Jan Žižka, one of the most successful military leaders in history. Directed by Czech filmmaker Petr Jákl, it provides a rare glimpse into Central European history without being filtered through the usual Western lens. Though not without its flaws, the film delivers a gripping tale of action and political intrigue, set in a region too often overlooked by cinema. Žižka, a warrior who defied imperialist powers — much as we Lamangese have — stands out as a true revolutionary and a figure worth admiring. A strong recommendation. 8/10 Fun with Girls What do you get when you cross Prince Charles and Queen Elizabeth? Dead in a tunnel.

raw.name: Newspaper - Capture of a Traitor
raw.transcript: Capture of a Traitor April 19, 2024 The secret services have successfully apprehended and repatriated the notorious traitor and enemy of the state, Thavisouk Saysanasy. “We are proud to confirm the capture of Thavisouk Saysanasy,” declared Vice President Jan Park. “A descendant of those who betrayed our nation during the so-called liberalization era, he had been hiding in Bangkok. But we found him. There is no safe haven for enemies of our Republic.” Nothing brings greater pride to the people than witnessing the downfall of their enemies. Apology for Error In our recent review of the film Civil War, our critic Nok Dam mistakenly failed to note that the director, Alex Garland, is of British origin. We sincerely apologize to any readers who may have attended the screening without being aware of this important detail. In light of this correction, the rating of the film has been revised from 7/10 to 6/10. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh It seems many believe that living abroad gives them the freedom to slander our beloved country without consequence. That is a grave mistake. We showed restraint in the case of Thavisouk Saysanasy. He was not one of the former oppressors who served the usurper Bounnhang Sayasone, but merely a descendant of those traitors who fled the moment the righteous people reclaimed control of our nation. The sins of the father do not automatically belong to the son, but Thavisouk committed his own. This mongrel, Lamangese only on one side, chose to spread lies about a country he has never even seen with his own eyes. Now, at last, he has the chance to witness firsthand the very nation he sought to undermine. A nation built on democracy that will not tolerate slander. Thailand may be displeased by our actions, but it must be understood: what we did was just and necessary. Film Review by Nok Dam — The Ministry of Ungentlemanly Warfare I want to apologize once again for my recent mistake; it will not happen again. The Ministry of Ungentlemanly Warfare is a quintessentially British film, featuring an ensemble of British actors, the familiar brand of British humor, and the heavy hand of British director Guy Ritchie. It tells an action-packed story of fighting the Nazis during the Second World War, glorifying the Western contribution while conveniently overlooking the immense sacrifices of the Red Army on the Eastern Front. 4/10 Fun with Girls Why do crabs never volunteer? Because they're shell-fish.

raw.name: Newspaper - Civil War Erupts in Lamang
raw.transcript: Civil War Erupts in Lamang July 20, 1968 Just weeks before the 20th anniversary of Lamang’s independence, a brutal civil war has broken out in the Southeast Asian nation. “We are engaged in a battle against a terrorist group known as the Sons of Lamang,” stated President Bounnhang Sayasone. “They are radical remnants of the anti-British resistance, driven by an extremist ideology that completely rejects Western values, which they view as fundamentally incompatible with our culture. Our armed forces are advancing steadily, and we are hopeful that this subversive group will be defeated before our August anniversary.” Available reports indicate that the Sons of Lamang primarily operate in jungle regions and are led by a figure named Raksmei Sayavong. As the conflict unfolds, hopes remain high that the violence will soon come to an end and peace will return to Lamang. Southeast Asia Gripped by the Spread of Communism As the war in Vietnam continues to escalate, communist insurgencies are gaining momentum in neighboring countries, threatening to overthrow legitimate governments through armed rebellion. Laos, Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand, the Philippines, and Indonesia — few nations in the region have been spared from clashes with communist forces. The question now is: will Lamang become the next battleground in this growing revolution? Interview — Brian J. Bronstein, Ph. D. Q: Dr. Bronstein, can you describe the current situation in Lamang? A: The rebel group known as the Sons of Lamang has launched an open offensive against the democratic government. Previously, they held control over some remote jungle regions and carried out sporadic guerrilla attacks, but their activity was relatively limited. It now appears they were stockpiling resources and preparing for a larger, more coordinated assault. Q: Why didn’t the government take more decisive action earlier? A: They made efforts, but the Lamang military has never been well-organized or equipped to deal with guerrilla-style warfare. Q: Do you believe the current government will survive this crisis? A: It's difficult to say. This is the most serious challenge to Lamang's statehood since it gained independence. Q: Thank you for your insights, Dr. Bronstein. A: You're very welcome. Letters to the Editor Hello, I found your piece on liberalization in Czechoslovakia really interesting. One of my ancestors came from there. I hope and pray that the people will be able to free themselves from the communist dictatorship. Richard S. Dear Richard, We’re glad you enjoyed our report on Czechoslovakia’s ongoing liberalization. Like you, we wish that the transition continues peacefully. Hopefully, we won’t see a repeat of what happened in Hungary in 1956.

raw.name: Newspaper - Covid Hits Lamang Hard
raw.transcript: Covid Hits Lamang Hard June 6, 2020 The Democratic Republic of Lamang is struggling to contain the rapid spread of COVID-19. Reports suggest thousands have died and many more are infected. “I can guarantee you we have no issue with this so-called disease. If you in the West are having a problem, that’s on you; don’t project it onto us. We’re completely fine,” said Vice President Jan Park in response to our questions. The true scale of the crisis in Lamang is difficult to determine, but given the regime’s track record in handling emergencies, it’s safe to assume they are facing serious problems. Poland Invades Czech Republic! For several days, a small Czech chapel near the Czech–Polish border was inadvertently occupied by the Polish army. Once higher authorities became aware of the situation, they promptly issued an apology and withdrew from Czech territory. Interview — Patricia Bell, Ph.D. Q: Dr. Bell, what can you tell us about the current situation in Lamang? A: It seems the Lamangese government has badly underestimated the threat of COVID-19. In that sense, it’s quite similar to North Korea. They’ll almost certainly blame the outside world for their own mistakes and lack of preparation. Sadly, it’s the ordinary people who will bear the consequences. Q: Do you think they’ll ask for help? A: No, they won’t. Authoritarian regimes like Lamang’s must project strength at all times. And even if, by some miracle, they accept assistance, they’ll present it as if it were their own act of generosity. Q: Do you expect many casualties in Lamang? A: Unfortunately, yes. Lamang has never had a large population, and this outbreak could further reduce the already small number of inhabitants. Q: Thank you for sharing your insights, Dr. Bell. A: You’re very welcome. Letters to the Editor Why won’t you report on the fantastic effects of disinfectants against covid??!!!!! Grady S. Dear Grady, Because we’re not insane.

raw.name: Newspaper - Disappearance of Stuart Kupferhower
raw.transcript: Disappearance of Stuart Kupferhower December 5, 2025 The UNLRA claims it successfully evacuated the population of Lamang. However, reports suggest that many people were left behind. Among the missing are numerous tourists — including Stuart Kupferhower, heir to a billion-dollar coal mining fortune. “Our son went to Lamang seeking fun and adventure, but since November 24, the day of the Event, we haven’t heard a word from him,” said Amanda Kupferhower, his mother. “The last time we spoke, he was preparing for a hike in the mountains. Please, if you have any information about my son, contact my assistant. If it turns out to be true, we will reward you with $100,000.” The fate of the missing remains unclear. So far, the UN has offered no official comment. Lamang Opposition Leader Arrested Kaysone Phouma, a prominent opposition figure, was detained while attempting to enter Lamang illegally, despite the ongoing UN-imposed quarantine. Q: Dr. Bell, what can you tell us about the rumors that the UNLRA left people behind in Lamang? A: If those reports are accurate, it would be a major scandal for the UN. They declared the mission a success, but it now seems they may not have done a very thorough job. Q: Do you think the UN might launch another rescue mission? A: Honestly, no. Even if people are still there, sending another mission would mean lifting the island’s quarantine, and from what we know, the UN is strongly opposed to that. We don’t yet understand why, but it might be connected to the Event. Q: You’ve been vocal about the theory that some bomb, possibly even nuclear, was used in Lamang. Do you believe the UN is hiding the truth? A: I don’t want to sound like a conspiracy theorist, but some of the UN’s actions do raise questions. There’s definitely something they’re not telling us. Q: Thank you for your time and insights, Dr. Bell. A: My pleasure. Letters to the Editor Hello, Why do you refer to the Democratic Republic of Lamang as a dictatorship? As a proud citizen of this beautiful country, I find it upsetting to hear my nation described in that way. Faydank Ch. Dear Faydank, If you're genuinely a concerned citizen of Lamang, I suggest you take an honest look at how dictatorships function and then ask yourself whether your government fits that pattern. But let’s be honest: it’s more likely you’re just another voice from Lamang's propaganda machine.

raw.name: Newspaper - Dissolution of the Soviet Union
raw.transcript: Dissolution of the Soviet Union December 27, 1991 With heavy hearts, we witness a historic turning point that will forever alter the global balance of power. The imperialists now stand without opposition, and the world enters an uncertain new era. “We must be ready to face the challenges ahead, for we no longer have our mighty ally by our side. The Soviet instructors stationed here in Lamang will soon return to their motherland to support their people in this difficult time. But do not fear, my fellow citizens. We are strong, as we proved when we triumphed over the British. If history dares to repeat itself, we shall emerge victorious once again,” declared President Raksmei Sayavong. We extend our deepest gratitude to our leader for his words of reassurance, and we thank the Soviet people who stood beside us in rebuilding our nation and helping to raise it to new heights. Workers React Grief echoes across Lamang as the nation mourns the loss of a brother state. “We, the workers, feel as though we have lost a member of our own family. The USSR stood with us when we reclaimed our homeland, and now we bid farewell to a cherished ally. May the Soviet workers remain safe in these uncertain times,” said a representative of the workers’ union. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh Our ally has fallen. It always seemed the USSR would stand with us forever. But, like a tale from Russian literature, the Soviet Union has met a tragic end. The imperialists have done it; they brought down their greatest adversary. No doubt Washington and London are celebrating wildly, convinced they’ve won the Cold War. They probably believe the whole world now belongs to them — these damn Anglo-Saxons. But the world is shifting, and their illusion of power will fade. The struggle for independence among the oppressed will continue. Imperialist guns and tanks do not intimidate the proud nations of this earth. Still, the world has lost a peaceful nation that once worked to preserve balance. Farewell, comrades. You will be remembered. Film Review by Nok Dam — The Last Boy Scout The Last Boy Scout delivers a modern twist on classic noir. The leads share strong chemistry, and their rapid-fire dialogue paired with explosive action keeps the pace relentless from start to finish. As with much of Hollywood, and Western society as a whole, the film reflects a deeply flawed system, incapable of protecting its people and drowning in corruption. Once again, it falls to a broken, disillusioned detective to impose justice. Despite being directed by a Brit, this film is genuinely entertaining. I highly recommend it. 9/10 Fun with Girls What do you call a magician who loses his magic? Ian.

raw.name: Newspaper - Election Results
raw.transcript: Election Results February 21, 2021 With great pride, we share the results of the 2021 elections. In what was described as a tightly contested race, an overwhelming 95% of voters cast their ballots for the Lamang Democratic Party. “We’re deeply grateful for the continued trust in our vision,” said Vice President Jan Park. “It means the world to us that our fellow citizens see us as worthy representatives. We promise to keep working hard to make you proud. And to those of you who voted for our opponents, don’t worry. We certainly won’t hold it against you.” The resounding victory is a clear sign of unity and confidence in our nation’s future. Criminals Apprehended Shortly after the elections, authorities dismantled an organized criminal group operating across Lamang. “This operation is entirely unrelated to the election outcome,” assured police spokesperson Sao Yang. The swift action underscores the government’s ongoing commitment to law and order. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh The elections have concluded peacefully, with the Lamang Democratic Party securing another decisive victory to guide our nation for the next five years. It is truly inspiring to see the enduring trust our people place in a party that grew from the Sons of Lamang movement. Nowhere else in the world does faith in government run as deep as it does here. With 95% of voters voicing their support, the message is clear: our government is serving the people well — a fact that no doubt provokes envy in many Western nations. Do better, imperialists! Film Review by Nok Dam — Cherry Cherry is a bleak story following Tom Holland’s descent into drug addiction after serving in the military. It exposes the West’s hollow promises of opportunity and the grim reality of how it chews up and discards its youth. The film provides an unflinching look at a world we must never imitate. I strongly recommend watching it. And remember — our government does not abandon its people. It stands with us, always. 8/10 Fun with Girls What did the bison say to his son when he left the ranch? Bi-son.

raw.name: Newspaper - Friendship Among Nations
raw.transcript: Friendship Among Nations January 15, 1970 With great pride, we announce that our esteemed President, Raksmei Sayavong, has reached an important agreement with representatives of the USSR to assist in the modernization and industrialization of the Democratic Republic of Lamang. "The Soviet Union has long played a crucial role among the nations striving for liberation from colonial and imperialist oppression. They have consistently stood on the side of just and rightful people, and today is no exception. We are not blind to the actions of the United States in Southeast Asia. These aggressors, acting like gangsters above the law, wage war not only against the freedom fighters of Vietnam but also inflicting suffering on innocent civilians in Laos and Cambodia, who are not even parties to the conflict. The imperialists will stop at nothing. We learned our lesson with the British, and we won't wait for the US to come to our island. That is why I welcome this strengthening of our partnership with the USSR, an unshakable stronghold against the imperialist predators that seek to dominate the world." Military Exercise The largest military exercise in Lamang’s history has just concluded. “We are ready for any unforeseen challenges. No enemy will ever set foot on our soil and find us unprepared,” stated General Sangha Vang. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh A man cannot survive alone, and the same is true for nations. Though we are a strong and independent country, hungry sharks still circle beyond our borders, waiting for any sign of weakness to strike. But unity brings strength. That is why we proudly declare to the world that we have entered into a friendship with the largest nation on Earth — the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics. The Soviets are not like the British, Japanese, or Americans. They do not seek to colonize us or dictate our path. Instead, they stand with us as equals, encouraging us to grow, prosper, and realize our full potential. And for that reason, this friendship shall endure. We salute our wise and visionary President Raksmei Sayavong, whose leadership has secured this historic alliance, bringing lasting strength and prosperity to Lamang. Film Review by Nok Kao — Patton This war movie lionizes the imperialist General George S. Patton, who led U.S. forces during World War II. Though it makes a superficial attempt to present him as a layered character, the narrative ultimately glorifies aggression, arrogance, and blind patriotism. Although the lead actor gives a powerful performance, the film’s underlying message is too steeped in Western militaristic fantasy to resonate with audiences who haven’t had their brains numbed by cola and popcorn. 5/10 Lonely Hearts Young Lady A young woman, who has assumed responsibility for a well-established restaurant near Tiger Bay due to her parents’ illness and old age, seeks engagement with a young restaurateur willing to take over the business and continue its traditions. Matchmakers are excluded. Further details are available through the administration of The Voice of Lamang.

raw.name: Newspaper - Friendship with the USSR in Perpetuity
raw.transcript: Friendship with the USSR in Perpetuity October 4, 1985 Thanks to our steadfast friendship and trade partnership with the Soviet Union, Lamang continues to prosper. There is no doubt we chose correctly when we rejected the empty promises of the Yankees — distant cousins of the despised British. “Our friendship with the USSR is unbreakable,” declared President Raksmei Sayavong. “While Western nations scorn us out of fear of true freedom, the Soviet Union respects our sovereignty and pride. Like the USSR, we stand with all freedom-loving and oppressed peoples in their fight to break free from Western colonialism.” His words remind us whom we can trust — and whom we must never forget to watch. The bond between Lamang and the USSR is more than political; it is a shared vision. And this friendship will endure for generations to come. Man Ate His Roommate's Duck, Who in Return Stole His Motorcycle Police in Nam Thaven recently handled an unusual dispute between two roommates. After one man discovered his favorite delicacy had gone missing, he decided to take matters into his own hands by stealing his roommate's motorcycle. The theft was reported to authorities, and after police intervention, the bike was eventually returned. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh It is a beautiful sight to witness the blossoming of true friendship, especially when that bond is between Lamang and the USSR. There is comfort in knowing we can count on those who see the world as we do. We endured bitter experiences under the British, just as the Soviets have long endured hostility from the capitalist West, which has sought to undermine them from the very beginning. Some believed the Soviets would abandon us after the Vietnam War, once we were no longer useful. But they have proven otherwise. Unlike the colonizers, they do not forget those who stood with them. To have allies such as the Soviets is a privilege. There is no doubt: this is a friendship destined to last forever. Film Review by Nok Dam — Commando Commando is a high-octane action film starring Arnold Schwarzenegger as John Matrix, a former special forces colonel whose daughter is kidnapped by a vengeful ex-dictator from South America. The story is a relentless thrill ride as Matrix races against time to rescue her, delivering one of Schwarzenegger’s most memorable performances. The film is filled with iconic one-liners, explosive set pieces, and brutal fight scenes. It also offers a critique of the failures of U.S. institutions to protect their own citizens, though at the same time it falls into caricaturing South American leaders. Don’t sleep on this one, it’s a true action masterpiece. 9/10 Fun with Girls Who won the neck decorating contest? It was a tie.

raw.name: Newspaper - Glorious Leader Narith Sayavong Celebrates 50th Birthday
raw.transcript: Glorious Leader Narith Sayavong Celebrates 50th Birthday August 1, 2018 Today marks the 50th birthday of our beloved President, Narith Sayavong, and the entire nation of Lamang is united in celebration of this historic occasion. Thousands have filled the streets with joy, honoring this monumental day. “What a time to be alive,” said one jubilant citizen, smiling from ear to ear. “Today I had the chance to close a deal that could have changed my family’s future forever. But what could possibly matter more than celebrating the birthday of our beloved President, Narith Sayavong?” A truly extraordinary day for all of Lamang. Even visitors from abroad have come to witness this moment firsthand and extend their congratulations to our glorious leader. May President Narith Sayavong live to be 200 years old! Pardon Granted As part of the birthday celebrations, President Narith Sayavong has shown his compassion by granting a full pardon to all individuals apprehended in July, provided their crimes did not involve murder. “The President is merciful. Glory to him,” said Thongloun Vatthana, convicted of corruption related to municipal housing, upon hearing the announcement. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh What a day to be alive! Our glorious leader, President Narith Sayavong, is celebrating his 50th birthday. I feel truly blessed to witness this historic moment, as does the entire nation of Lamang. Children wave flags, adults march with banners, and the streets of every city and town are alive with joy as people honor our heroic President. It is a moving sight: one nation, united in pride and celebration. With hope and devotion, we look forward to the day when we celebrate our beloved leader’s 100th birthday. Congratulations, President Narith Sayavong, our protector, our defender, our guiding light. Film Review by Nok Dam — Mission: Impossible – Fallout Mission: Impossible – Fallout is an entertaining and well-crafted film. 8/10 Yet no matter how thrilling the action on screen may be, it pales in comparison to the true event of the day. The 50th birthday of our esteemed President, Narith Sayavong. It is thanks to his wise leadership that our nation prospers, and today, we join together to honor him on this special occasion. Let us celebrate and extend our heartfelt congratulations to our beloved President. We love you, dearest President. May happiness and good fortune follow you with every step. Fun with Girls Can a frog jump higher than a house? Of course, a house can't jump.

raw.name: Newspaper - Honoring the Best Workers
raw.transcript: Honoring the Best Workers May 2, 2016 A day to remember. Each year, on the eve of Labour Day, comes a tradition that leaves a lasting mark — the honoring of the nation’s finest workers by President Narith Sayavong. Long before the ceremony began, the corridor linking the Representation Room to Parliament was alive with energy. Nominees for honorary titles, state decorations, and national awards gathered with visible excitement and anticipation. “I can’t wait to shake hands with our beloved President. I’ll be telling my grandchildren about this,” said Wai Lor, a construction worker from Chon village, beaming with pride. The Voice of the People Echoed Across the Nation: Our Security Lies in the Party’s Policy! May Day was celebrated across Lamang as a testament to the joyful lives of workers. President Narith Sayavong delivered a stirring and unforgettable speech, reflecting on the nation’s turbulent past while promising a radiant future for every worker. His words resonated deeply, moving citizens to tears in every corner of the country. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh There is no day more meaningful to workers than Labor Day. For the individuals and groups chosen to meet our esteemed President Narith Sayavong, it is truly a life-changing experience. We all know of the President’s extraordinary achievements, but seeing him in person is something entirely different. The heroic figure we read about or hear in speeches becomes real before our very eyes. It feels as though a higher being has stepped down to walk among us. I cannot help but envy those meeting the President for the first time. I would give anything to relive that moment. Film Review by Nok Dam — The Nice Guys The Nice Guys is an entertaining ride from legendary writer-director Shane Black. This detective buddy comedy follows Russell Crowe and Ryan Gosling as they navigate through a chaotic and genuinely engaging mystery. If you’re looking for a fun film that doesn’t try to be more than it is, I wholeheartedly recommend it. 8/10 Fun with Girls I got a new pen that can write underwater. It can write other words too.

raw.name: Newspaper - Horrors of the Survivors
raw.transcript: Horrors of the Survivors December 13, 2025 Reports from Lamang refugees grow more disturbing by the day. Allegations presented to the United Nations are not only being confirmed but often turn out to be even worse than initially described. Survivors paint a picture of Lamang as a living hell, where human life was treated as less valuable than that of insects. “It was unbearable. It felt like we were imprisoned our entire lives,” said refugee Siluck Suriyajak. “I’ve had anxiety since childhood. Now, for the first time, I feel like I can finally breathe. I no longer have to live in fear that saying the wrong thing could get me reported to the secret police by my neighbor.” The hope now is that refugees will be able to overcome their trauma and rebuild their lives in countries that do not terrorize their own citizens. UN Remains Silent The United Nations has declined to comment on the situation in Lamang. An official inquiry was submitted, but no response had been received by the time of publication. Interview — Kaysone Phouma Q: Mr. Phouma, as the leader of the Lamang opposition in exile, what is your perspective on the current events? A: It's a disgrace that the UN failed to act sooner. We've been warning them for years about the regime’s oppressive tactics and shady dealings. Now there’s been an explosion that shook the entire island, likely caused by Narith Sayavong himself, and the vast majority of the population has been forced to evacuate. Q: You were recently arrested while attempting to go to Lamang. Why did you want to go there? A: Because I want to witness the fall of the regime with my own eyes. I want to help rebuild my homeland and drive out the evil that has ruled it for decades. I also want to support those left behind by UNLRA, people who have no one else. They need leadership, compassion, and a path to survival in a country that no longer functions. Q: Lamang is known for its long-reigning presidents — Bounnhang Sayasone, Raksmei Sayavong, and Narith Sayavong. Are you also planning to pursue the presidency? A: Don’t compare President Bounnhang Sayasone to the others. Yes, he served for many years, but always within the boundaries of the constitution, and he won fair elections. As the leader of the exiled opposition, I will naturally run for president. But I won’t impose anything on the people. There will be free and fair elections. That’s a promise. Q: Thank you for your time and insights, Mr. Phouma. A: You’re welcome. Free Lamang! Letters to the Editor Good day, I want to thank you for your report on Lamang. Most newspapers barely mention the country, if at all, and when they do, it's buried somewhere on page five. Carl C. Dear Carl, Thank you for your kind letter. It’s refreshing to hear from readers who aren’t trolls or conspiracy theorists! We genuinely appreciate your support. We'll continue to do our best to bring you precise and reliable global news.

raw.name: Newspaper - Insurrection Averted!
raw.transcript: Insurrection Averted! September 22, 2002 The British imperialists have never forgiven us for driving them out of our homeland. Their bitterness endures, and even decades later, they continue to meddle in our affairs, hoping to corrupt the good citizens of Lamang. Sadly, not all among us have the strength to resist the seductive pull of imperialist gold. What began as a seemingly routine strike by timber workers in the island's eastern region quickly escalated into a full-blown rebellion. Fueled by Western influence and greed, the traitorous rebels turned their weapons against riot police, spilling the blood of their fellow countrymen. Leading this treacherous uprising was fraudster Lani Sayavong, who has long benefited from the undeserved prestige of sharing a surname with our revered leaders. But his days of impunity are over. Thanks to the swift and courageous action of young commander Nuon Bintang, the rebellion was crushed in its infancy. Though a handful of rebels fled into the dense jungle, it won't be long before they are all caught and brought to justice, where they will receive a fair, yet merciless trial. Young Love Drama A teenage girl from Tiger Bay was arrested after she reportedly threatened her boyfriend with a kitchen knife. "She's crazy," said the young man, now her ex. "I wouldn't be surprised if she actually murdered someone one day." After spending the night in a police station, she was sent back to her parents. Authorities hope that this experience will serve as a wake-up call. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh Betrayal — there's no word more chilling. It wears many faces, but none more vile than treason. Treason against one's homeland. What kind of creature would sell itself to foreign powers and cast aside everything we've built together? Who, in their right mind, would willingly tear down their own beautiful country? Disagreement has its place. Debate is part of a healthy society. But the moment innocent lives are taken, a line is crossed. Unforgivable. These are not revolutionaries. They are terrorists. Mindless, destructive terrorists. We must root every last one out before this disease spreads. These parasites hiding among us cannot be ignored. It is your duty, as citizens, to act. Report these traitors, these wicked contra-revolutionaries. Help our nation get rid of these cockroaches before they drag you down with them. Film Review by Nok Dam — Ballistic: Ecks vs. Sever To the untrained eye, this might look like a standard action thriller. In truth, it plays more like an unintentional parody. Antonio Banderas and Lucy Liu are both talented, but even their star power can’t salvage this spectacular mess. Yes, there’s constant action and plenty of flashy explosions, but the film reeks of directionlessness. It's as if an overfunded amateur was handed the reins with no idea what to do. It's a shame that such a terrible thing was created by a fellow South Asian. 3/10 Fun with Girls How did the barber win the race? He knew a short cut.

raw.name: Newspaper - Lamang Awakens
raw.transcript: Lamang Awakens January 22, 2026 Despite the international quarantine, Lamang is far from silent. Persistent rumors suggest that several private military companies have managed, despite considerable difficulty, to breach the blockade and infiltrate the abandoned nation. One confirmed presence is the Lamang Recovery Initiative (LRI), a group that, according to its website, was founded to locate and assist any survivors left behind after the United Nations’ withdrawal. “We are finishing what the UN started. Due to the poorly executed evacuation by UNLRA, there are still vulnerable people left on the island. We refuse to let them die. That’s why we’re taking action, even if it goes against the UN’s wishes,” said an LRI spokesperson. Unverified reports also suggest the presence of other PMCs, including Mithras Security Systems (MSS) and Crimson Shield International (CSI). Neither company has commented on their alleged activities in Lamang. Despite the ongoing crisis, the national government of Lamang insists it remains in control. “We want to send a clear message to any international organizations or individuals foolish enough to try and steal from our nation: we are still here, and we will defend our land against any intruders. Do not come to Lamang. It is not safe for you,” stated Vice President Jan Park. Interview — Andrew Bennett, Ph.D. Q: Dr. Bennett, could you explain the role of PMCs in Lamang? A: Certainly. The power vacuum in Lamang has attracted a range of individuals and organizations looking to exploit the situation for their gain. Getting past the UN blockade is difficult, but certainly not impossible. These PMCs are clearly trying to secure whatever knowledge lies behind the Event for their employers, even if they try to disguise their presence as a \"humanitarian mission.\" Q: Do you have a hypothesis about what might have caused the massive explosion? A: I’m convinced it wasn’t any known weapon of mass destruction, despite what Dr. Bell and others have suggested. It was likely some experimental device… or perhaps something entirely unknown to us. Q: Are you implying it might have been extraterrestrial? We know you, like Avi Loeb, have supported the alien-origin hypothesis regarding the ʻOumuamua object. A: It could have been a device unfamiliar to the broader scientific community, one that either malfunctioned or worked precisely as intended. Lamang is a very secretive nation. That said, I wouldn't rule out the possibility of an extraterrestrial origin. PMCs wouldn’t be taking such risks if they didn’t believe the payoff would be truly extraordinary. Q: Thank you, Dr. Bennett. A: My pleasure. Stay open-minded. Letters to the Editor I’m getting fed up with all the news about Lamang. Isn’t there anything else happening in the world? Chris J. Dear Chris, Even when Lamang makes the front page, we continue to report on many other topics as well. You just need to conquer your fear of turning pages and read a bit beyond the cover.

raw.name: Newspaper - Lamang Escapees Speak Out
raw.transcript: Lamang Escapees Speak Out December 4, 2024 Escapees from the Democratic Republic of Lamang have come forward to share harrowing stories of the conditions they endured. The United Nations has received numerous testimonies and pieces of evidence detailing human rights abuses committed by the regime. "We’ve been warning about this for years. The current regime in Lamang resembles an organized crime syndicate more than a legitimate government,” said Kaysone Phouma, the exiled opposition leader. “Just a few months ago, regime agents abducted Thavisouk Saysanasy from his home in Bangkok. He was an outspoken critic of Narith Sayavong and his inner circle. To this day, we don’t know what happened to him. There are many similar cases still waiting to be uncovered, and we urge the UN to take meaningful action.” South Korea Martial Law South Korean President Yoon Suk-yeol declared martial law, citing security concerns. It was overturned just six hours later by a unanimous vote in the National Assembly. Interview — Andrew Bennett, Ph.D. Q: Dr. Bennett, could you explain the increasing number of escapee testimonies from Lamang? A: It's a fascinating and troubling trend. Lamang has crafted a glamorous image in the West to attract wealthy tourists; traveling there is remarkably easy. But beneath that veneer, it's a dictatorship that tightly controls who among its citizens can leave, much like the Iron Curtain during the Cold War era. The fact that more people are fleeing suggests conditions for ordinary citizens have become dire enough to risk everything. Q: What action can we expect from the UN? A: Honestly, it’s uncertain. The UN is often criticized for turning a blind eye, but the rising number of escapee accounts could force their hand. If the situation worsens, pressure will mount. Despite being authoritarian, Lamang relies heavily on tourism and won’t want to damage its global reputation. Still, that's a big if. Q: Do you believe Lamang could ever become a free nation? A: Well, in the past it was. From 1948 to 1968, it was a functioning democracy. That ended when Raksmei Sayavong seized power, and his family has ruled ever since, much like the Kims in North Korea. There is hope — opposition leader Kaysone Phouma is capable — but change would require a spark from within. Unfortunately, due to decades of isolation and propaganda, the Lamangese population on the island distrusts even its own people from the mainland. Q: Thank you, Dr. Bennett. A: My pleasure. Letters to the Editor You filthy scribblers, Why won't you interview Dr. Nathaniel Duke??!! He’s one of the brightest minds in U.S. history!!!! Amanda P. Dear Nathaniel, Next time you send fake fan mail, at least remember to use a different email address, you lousy conspiracy theorist. We don’t give space to con artists with forged Ph.D. credentials. And even if your degree were legitimate, let’s be honest — you have nothing meaningful to contribute beyond fringe ramblings. Now go sprinkle some vinegar in your backyard; a plane probably flew overhead.

raw.name: Newspaper - Lamang Secures Independence from British Rule
raw.transcript: Lamang Secures Independence from British Rule August 17, 1948 A small Southeast Asian nation has officially gained independence from the British, marking one of the many post–World War II victories in the wave of anti-colonial movements sweeping across the globe. “We are proud that our independence has been achieved without unnecessary violence. British officials are transferring authority peacefully, and we are gradually assuming control over the institutions required to govern our country,” stated Bounnhang Sayasone, leader of the anti-colonial opposition. However, not all is as seamless as it appears. Some factions within the anti-British opposition have voiced discontent with the pace and nature of the political transition. According to them, the changes unfolding in Lamang fall short of true reform. For now, the world watches with cautious optimism, hoping the following headlines from Lamang will speak of progress, and not internal conflict. Lamang–British History The British colonized the island of Lamang in 1824, beginning 124 years of colonial rule. Their policies prioritized the planting of tobacco, pepper, and, later, rubber trees. A colonial office was established with an appointed administrator, and the island was incorporated into British Malaya for administrative purposes. Interview — Brian J. Bronstein, Ph. D. Q: Dr. Bronstein, could you please describe what is currently happening in Lamang? A: Certainly. The anti-colonial forces in this small Southeast Asian nation have succeeded in their struggle against British rule and have successfully negotiated their independence. Q: Are the British upset about losing control of the territory? A: I don’t believe so. Lamang is relatively insignificant from both strategic and economic standpoints. It’s a small island, approximately 430 square kilometers in size, with no significant natural resources. If anything, the British are probably relieved to no longer be responsible for governing this remote island that was forcibly added to Malaya. Q: How do you see Lamang’s future? A: If current trends continue, Lamang could become one of the more stable nations in the developing world, provided it remains committed to upholding democratic principles. Q: Thank you for your time, Dr. Bronstein. A: My pleasure. Letters to the Editor Hello, Could you report on what’s happening in Korea? There seems to be some tension. Warm regards, Stanley L. Dear Stanley, You’re right, tensions are rising. On August 15, 1948, the Republic of Korea was officially established, an event that has clearly angered the Soviet Union. We’ll provide a more detailed report soon.

raw.name: Newspaper - Lamang’s Underworld Rising
raw.transcript: Lamang’s Underworld Rising February 8, 2023 Southeast Asia has long been associated with organized crime, particularly in the infamous Golden Triangle region spanning northeastern Myanmar, northwestern Thailand, and northern Laos. But recent investigations suggest the Democratic Republic of Lamang is emerging as a significant new player in the region’s criminal underworld. “It doesn’t surprise me that Western media are spreading lies about our country. We are a small nation focused on tourism, not crime,” said Vice President Jan Park in response to our inquiries. Despite his denial, evidence points to extensive drug and human trafficking operations, along with a surge in scam calls and digital fraud originating from Lamang. Increasingly, it appears the dictatorship may be using tourism as a façade to mask its criminal activities. Forced Labor in Lamang Although slavery is outlawed worldwide, Lamang continues to practice methods that strongly resemble it. Reports indicate that foreign workers arrive in Lamang seeking well-paid jobs, only to have their passports confiscated and be forced into labor, often working merely for food and water. Women are primarily coerced into prostitution, while men are exploited in construction and digital fraud schemes. Interview — Patricia Bell, Ph.D. Q: Dr. Bell, as an expert on Southeast Asia, what can you tell us about the current state of crime in Lamang? A: It’s extremely difficult to get a clear picture inside a closed-off country like Lamang. As with many authoritarian regimes, they make investigations nearly impossible and suppress information that might expose their wrongdoing. From what little we do know, they’ve likely struck some kind of arrangement with criminal networks operating out of the Golden Triangle. And that’s not even accounting for the other criminal activities happening within the country. Q: So you believe the Lamangese government is cooperating with Golden Triangle crime syndicates? A: Not necessarily in a direct sense, but certainly in an indirect one. I believe they rely on local criminal groups to carry out illicit operations, while the government maintains an appearance of defending traditional values and national order. Q: Is there any realistic way to hold them accountable? A: Unless you’re prepared to support military intervention, which I’m not suggesting, then unfortunately, no. For now, all we can do is wait. If the regime eventually collapses, there may be a window to uncover the truth and bring justice for the crimes committed. Q: Thank you for sharing your insights, Dr. Bell. A: You’re welcome. Letters to the Editor Why don’t you publish horoscopes in your newspaper? Samantha F. Dear Samantha, For the same reason, we don’t report on Santa Claus. We don't make things up.

raw.name: Newspaper - Mysteries Regarding The Event
raw.transcript: Mysteries Regarding The Event December 15, 2025 The Event, as the mysterious explosion in Lamang has come to be known, remains shrouded in secrecy. The UN has yet to provide an official explanation for the island’s total quarantine, and experts remain divided on its cause. “We’ve spoken with numerous refugees from Lamang, as well as tourists who were there at the time, and their accounts of The Event vary wildly. Some described strange phenomena in the sky, while others claimed to hear voices speaking directly to them. It’s all incredibly bizarre,” reported our correspondent from a refugee camp in Indonesia. For now, the true nature of The Event remains unknown. All that can be said with certainty is that whatever lies at Ground Zero, the epicenter of the blast, is being kept carefully hidden. Organized Crime Eyes Lamang According to reports, organized crime groups from neighboring countries have slipped through the UN quarantine. With the island abandoned and effectively lawless, Lamang now appears to be a golden opportunity for criminal enterprises. Interview — Andrew Bennett, Ph.D. Q: Dr. Bennett, what’s your hypothesis on why the accounts of The Event vary so drastically? A: It’s possible the explosion was chemical in nature, causing neurological effects in those exposed. Another theory is that it may have been some form of experimental cognitive weapon. Either way, the conflicting testimonies make research into The Event extremely challenging. Q: There are reports that criminal groups have infiltrated Lamang despite the UN quarantine. What should we expect from them? A: They’re drawn to Lamang like moths to a flame. With much of the country abandoned in a hurry, they’ll attempt to exploit the situation, looting unguarded homes and resources. Q: According to our sources, dictator Narith Sayavong and the Lamang military have not left the country. What does that suggest? A: They’ll likely concentrate on securing key areas. Sayavong has always ruled through fear, and I expect his regime will double down on violence and control in an attempt to stabilize the situation and reassert dominance over what remains of the population. Q: Thank you, Dr. Bennett. A: My pleasure. Letters to the Editor Hello, I’ve been following all the news about Lamang, and I don’t understand why the UN allowed people from the island to leave. We still don’t know what The Event really was. They could be carrying some unknown disease or something equally dangerous. Ava T. Dear Ava, The UNLRA has assured that all evacuees were thoroughly screened, and no evidence of disease or contamination linked to The Event has been found. Let’s avoid fueling unnecessary fear or panic.

raw.name: Newspaper - Mysterious Explosion
raw.transcript: Mysterious Explosion November 25, 2025 An unidentified explosion shook the island nation of Lamang late last night. Located in Southeast Asia, the Democratic Republic of Lamang is widely regarded as a reclusive, authoritarian state — often compared to North Korea — with the Sayavong family maintaining firm control. Due to longstanding reports of human rights abuses, the United Nations recently launched a humanitarian mission in the country. Given the scale of the blast, speculation is already circulating that it may have been either a nuclear test or a volcanic eruption. Authorities have yet to issue an official statement, and no further information is currently available. UNLRA Initiates Evacuation Effort Following a mysterious explosion on Lamang Island, the United Nations has launched a large-scale rescue operation. Neighboring mainland countries are preparing evacuation centers to accommodate the growing number of displaced people in urgent need of assistance. Interview — Prof. Jeremiah D. Archibald Q: Professor, could you share your thoughts on what might have caused the explosion in Lamang? A: At this stage, the possibilities are nearly limitless. Given the country’s secretive nature, we can only speculate. But considering the scale of the blast, it most likely could have been a volcanic eruption or a chemical plant explosion. Less likely possibilities include a nuclear detonation, a satellite crash, a meteorite impact, or some other rare Black Swan event. Q: There are also theories suggesting it may have had extraterrestrial origins. A: Ah yes, the ever-popular alien hypothesis. If I had a nickel for every time someone mentioned aliens in a situation like this, I’d be a billionaire by now. Personally, I think we can safely rule that one out. Q: So you believe the cause is likely something more natural? A: Most likely, yes. However, the truth is that we know very little about what’s happening inside Lamang. It’s an isolated dictatorship, and such regimes have a tendency to experiment with dangerous technologies behind closed doors. An internal weapons test or an experimental accident is, in my view, a far more likely scenario. Q: Thank you for your time, Professor. A: My pleasure. Letters to the Editor Hello, Why don't you report on the UNLRA's objectives in Lamang? Everybody knows their goal is to wipe out the population there with vaccines and take their oil. Thank you. Kevin M. Dear Kevin, We have previously reported on the UNLRA mission in Lamang. Their deployment aims to assist the local population facing challenging conditions. There are no forced vaccinations taking place, nor any plans to exploit oil resources, as the area does not have significant oil reserves. We recommend that you stop sniffing glue.

raw.name: Newspaper - Mysterious Lights
raw.transcript: Mysterious Lights August 17, 2020 Strange lights have been spotted around Ban Pa, a remote village on the eastern side of the island long wrapped in mystery. Eyewitnesses claim to have seen ghostly figures and other supernatural phenomena in the area, adding to the region's eerie reputation. “We’re not entirely sure what people may have witnessed,” said Vice President Jan Park. “But we strongly advise both citizens and tourists to stay away from Ban Pa and its surroundings. The local residents are known to be unfriendly toward outsiders, and the area remains hazardous due to abandoned Japanese-era structures—possibly even old land mines and unexploded ordnance.” Ban Pa has become something of a legend in our nation, and its secrets continue to spark curiosity. However, people should really avoid this place as much as they can. Twelve Hours of Horror and Despair A terrifying incident occurred near Kiu Vongsa, where an elderly woman became trapped under a tree root after a fall. In shock and completely exhausted, she lost her voice and was unable to call for help, even as people searched for her nearby. “It was horrible… I was there for twelve hours,” said Nang Lee, her voice still shaking. Thankfully, the ordeal ended on a positive note. Nang was eventually found and rescued, suffering only minor bruises and a few scratches. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh Many myths circulate throughout our nation — tales of ancient idols, vengeful spirits, monsters lurking in the woods, and long-lost treasures. We're not alone in this; much of Southeast Asia shares a rich tradition of similar folklore. They say every legend holds a sliver of truth, and perhaps that's true. But more often than not, these supernatural tales have down-to-earth explanations. People lost in the deep jungle may have fallen victim to bandits. The traveler who survived the fall wasn't saved by a forest spirit but rather by plain luck. And the ghosts are often nothing more than projections of a guilty conscience. Storytelling is a deeply human instinct. Today, we invent new myths, for example, about aliens watching from the skies or hidden Japanese storage caves — modern echoes of old tales about gods and treasures. Imagination knows no bounds, and sometimes it veers into the absurd. People will even spread horrifying stories about our fair and just state, just because they were fined for speeding. Film Review by Nok Dam — Wonder Woman 1984 Wonder Woman 1984 is a colorful spectacle, but nothing more. Gal Gadot attempts to embody a mythic heroine, yet her character spends more time in shopping malls than facing meaningful conflict. The film lacks any real struggle unless we count the viewer’s struggle to finish watching it. The first Wonder Woman was better. 4/10 Fun with Girls Why are frogs always so happy? They eat whatever bugs them.

raw.name: Newspaper - National Cuisine in Tiger Bay Central
raw.transcript: National Cuisine in Tiger Bay Central September 6, 2023 A grand food festival was held in Tiger Bay Central, bringing together chefs from across the country to showcase their finest dishes. All competed for the coveted title of Best Chef in Lamang, along with the prize money. Our esteemed leader, President Narith Sayavong, together with Vice President Jan Park, honored the event with their presence. “It’s truly wonderful to see so many people, especially visitors from abroad, coming to Tiger Bay Central to experience the best cuisine our island has to offer,” President Sayavong remarked. The winner was a chef from the renowned Temple Restaurant, receiving the prize directly from the President himself. As part of his reward, he was also promised a place in the shopping mall. We extend our congratulations to the winning chef and our gratitude to the President for making this occasion unforgettable. Police Warning The police issue a strict warning to all citizens: leaving the country without official permission is a serious crime. Any attempt to cross the border illegally will result in immediate arrest and severe punishment. “We have already detained individuals, including entire families, who thought they could escape the law,” said police spokesman Sao Yang. “Let this be a clear message, no one will succeed. Do not risk your future, or the future of your family. Our prisons are full, but we will always find room for traitors.” Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh I’ve never tasted better food than what we have here in Lamang. In my travels around the world, I’ve tried every cuisine imaginable — French, Italian, Indian, Japanese, Thai, American, and yes, even the foul excuse for food served by the British. Some of those flavors still make me shudder. But no national cuisine compares to the treasure we have in our own country. Here in Lamang, we cook with something no one else seems to understand: true love. Our food embodies the spirit of family, deep bonds, and care passed from one generation to the next. While much of the world treats food as just a business, focused on profit and branding, we approach it differently. We strive for perfection not because we expect a reward, but because we genuinely care for one another. Film Review by Nok Dam — Blue Beetle Blue Beetle is yet another unnecessary entry in the bloated superhero genre, built around a second-rate hero. After graduation, Jaime Reyes becomes host to an alien biotech scarab that grants him powers. What follows is a predictable story about battling an evil corporation — ironically produced by a corporation trying to milk the last drops out of the superhero craze. Not worth your time, or any further words. 3/10 Fun with Girls My barber said he can't cut my hair any longer. He can only cut it shorter.

raw.name: Newspaper - Never Again!
raw.transcript: Never Again! February 14, 2024 Today marks exactly 200 years since one of the darkest chapters in Lamang’s history — when our homeland was seized and turned into a British colony. At the time, we did not fully understand what was happening. We were unwillingly forced into servitude by foreign rulers from a distant island, thousands of kilometers away, who claimed the right to decide our fate. It took many years — and countless sacrifices — before we broke free and reclaimed our sovereignty. But every struggle was worth it when we look at the Lamang of today, and all we have achieved under the leadership of President Narith Sayavong. “We are a people who cherish peace and stability. But we will never again allow our country to be enslaved. We will defend it with whatever we have — and if it comes to it, we will fight with our fists and our teeth,” said Vice President Jan Park. We fully stand by his words. Should our sovereignty ever again be threatened, there is no doubt that the people of Lamang will rise as one to defend our nation from any would-be usurpers. Let history be our witness: Lamang will never kneel again! Death to the Enemies of Liberty Across towns and villages throughout the nation, the people of Lamang raise their voices in pride as the Union Jack burns. “We were meant to stay on standby today,” said Malaithong Sisoulith, chief of the eastern fire department, “but when we saw the British flags set ablaze, we couldn’t help but join in.” Everyone is doing their part. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh I’m deeply proud to see our country steadily moving away from its colonial legacy. Today, many ordinary citizens can hardly speak English anymore — and that’s a remarkable achievement. It took major education reforms and a great deal of sacrifice, but we’ve done it. We’ve returned to our roots. I feel a surge of pride when I walk through our cities and hear, almost exclusively, our native language instead of the tongue of our former oppressors. On this sombre anniversary, it’s significant that this linguistic shift is now nearly complete. To my fellow citizens: do not let yourselves be lured back into the trap of the English language. Let the burden of learning and using that cursed tongue fall to politicians, scientists, businesspeople, and their families. You should take joy in speaking your mother tongue freely and proudly. Film Review by Nok Dam — Madame Web Madame Web is a muddled Marvel spinoff that struggles under a convoluted script, uninspired direction, and a full-blown tonal identity crisis. While Dakota Johnson delivers occasional moments of muted charm, the film is bogged down by heavy exposition, sloppy effects, and a lack of coherent vision. This movie serves as yet another reminder that, for all their dazzling technology, Western imperialists remain ideologically bankrupt. As such, it is but another shiny distraction from a culture in decline. 2/10 Fun with Girls The sun never set on the British Empire because even God didn’t trust them in the dark.

raw.name: Newspaper - New Playground for the Elite
raw.transcript: New Playground for the Elite January 13, 2025 The latest hotspot for wealthy travelers is the Midnight Sapphire Resort in the Democratic Republic of Lamang. Since opening in 2015, this luxurious retreat in the small Southeast Asian nation has been drawing attention, with Hollywood stars praising the locals’ \"generosity\" and the \"modern\" hospitality they’ve experienced. “The glorification of authoritarian regimes like Lamang, and the willful ignorance of the suffering endured by their citizens, is a recurring affliction in Western societies, particularly among the elite,” said Dr. Patricia Bell, an expert on Southeast Asia. “As long as their fantasies are indulged, many are willing to overlook grave injustices. Just consider the example of Jeffrey Epstein.” The Democratic Republic of Lamang is, by all accounts, a dictatorship under Narith Sayavong, who took power in 1996 after the suspicious death of his father, Raksmei Sayavong, in a car accident. Since then, Narith has gradually opened the country to tourism. Before praising Lamang as a luxury escape, one might ask: is your vacation truly worth the price of another’s oppression? Indonesia joins BRICS Indonesia has officially become a full member of BRICS, making it the first Southeast Asian nation to join the intergovernmental organization. Interview — Patricia Bell, Ph.D. Q: Dr. Bell, could you explain the growing popularity of Lamang among tourists? A: The credit largely goes to Narith Sayavong, who began opening up the country shortly after his father’s death. With the fall of the Soviet Union, Lamang lost a significant source of financial support, particularly from Soviet intelligence operations based there during the Vietnam War. After the Soviets withdrew in 1991, the country experienced prolonged economic stagnation. When Narith came to power, he aimed to reverse that by transforming Lamang into a luxury destination for the wealthy. His goal was to attract foreign money to sustain both the country’s economy and his regime’s less savory activities. Q: Lamang is still considered a mysterious destination. What is it actually like there? A: The Democratic Republic of Lamang is, in essence, a reactionary dictatorship. The appearance of openness to tourists, especially the elite, is more of a public relations strategy than genuine reform. They’re selling curated dreams while masking the everyday oppression faced by the local population. Visually and culturally, Lamang resembles some of its Southeast Asian neighbors, most closely Laos, with whom it shares linguistic ties. Expect tropical jungles, rice paddies, and a humid, hot climate. Q: So, would you advise against traveling there? A: Absolutely — not just for ethical reasons, but also for safety concerns. There have been numerous reports of tourists disappearing. The only relatively safe place is the ultra-exclusive Midnight Sapphire Resort, built specifically to cater to the super-rich. Beyond its gates, the risk increases dramatically, as organized crime operates with impunity in parts of Lamang. Q: Thank you for your insights, Dr. Bell. A: You’re very welcome. Letters to the Editor Dear Worldview News, I've noticed that some of your news stories are reported with a few days’ delay. Is there a specific reason for this (censorship)? Thank you for your response, Boris C. Dear Boris, Of course, there may be instances where a delay occurs in reporting certain information. As a global news outlet, we cover events from all over the world, and occasionally, this can result in delays in reporting due to the complexity and volume of information we handle. Don't read too much into it. Rest assured, no censorship is involved. We are committed to accuracy, transparency, and journalistic integrity.

raw.name: Newspaper - Opening of Fort Raksmei
raw.transcript: Opening of Fort Raksmei May 2, 1975 A new symbol of unbreakable revolutionary strength has risen on the sacred soil of the homeland. Under the extraordinary guidance of President Raksmei Sayavong, the inauguration ceremony of a newly constructed modern fort was held yesterday with great revolutionary fervor. This impenetrable fortress stands as a bulwark of our military might, a shining testament to the outstanding achievements of President Raksmei Sayavong, who continues to lead the Lamang people on the path of self-reliance, defense, and victory. In a congratulatory message, President Raksmei Sayavong praised the patriotic devotion of the soldiers, engineers, workers, and USSR consultants who labored tirelessly to complete this historic project ahead of schedule. End of a Traitor In the early hours of the morning, General Sangha Vang was executed by hanging for crimes of treason. "I am deeply ashamed of the actions I took. My moral weakness brought loss and sorrow upon my country," the General said in his final statement. "I pray that my death may wash the shame that has befallen my family." Following his execution, the former General’s widow and two daughters were transferred to the Homphu Suk labor camp for political reeducation. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh To be truly free, a nation must first be strong. The world does not respect those who cannot defend themselves. That is why it is essential that we strengthen our military by any means necessary. We must be relentless in our mission to turn our island into an impenetrable fortress — one that no imperialist power would dare to challenge. The construction of Fort Raksmei is a vital step toward that vision. A modern military base of this scale will send a clear message: we are not to be underestimated. Yet an army is only as strong as the people within it. And if we cannot trust our defenders, how can they protect us? The case of General Sangha Vang has revealed a hard truth: even in our new and thriving society, corruption and betrayal can still take root. For some, no amount of prosperity is ever enough. We must remain vigilant against such opportunists who would trade their honor for thirty pieces of silver. Our future depends on it. Film Review by Nok Kao — Death Race 2000 Death Race 2000 is a grim reflection of capitalist decadence disguised as entertainment. The story is set in a dystopian future where pedestrians are run over for points and the amusement of the viewers. Though advertised as satire, any discerning viewer will recognize that this is less a parody and more a reflection of where the imperialist United States is headed. A nation obsessed with conflict, spectacle, and manufactured drama is bound to produce something similar to what is depicted in this disgusting film. 4/10 Lonely Hearts Marriage Proposal A 32-year-old widower with stable employment in public service seeks a lifelong companion. Due to limited personal time, I am pursuing this path to find a sincere and lasting relationship. Only genuine inquiries should be directed to the administration of The Voice of Lamang, labeled under "Serious Relationship.

raw.name: Newspaper - Paradise Found
raw.transcript: Paradise Found November 14, 2025 In a recent interview, Lamang’s Vice President Jan Park addressed international critics who have likened our nation to North Korea. Park dismissed the comparisons as unfounded and invited the world to experience the truth for themselves. "I don’t understand why Lamang is being compared to a closed-off country like North Korea," Park remarked. "We are not a nation of secrecy or isolation. We are a land of open arms and warm smiles. Anyone who visits will see for themselves that Lamang is closer to paradise on earth than anywhere else in the world." It's hard to argue with Park's claim. Lamang boasts an abundance of breathtaking tourist attractions that rival the world's most famous destinations. For example, the wildly beautiful Blue Lagoon offers a serene escape for nature lovers. The luxurious Midnight Sapphire Resort provides unparalleled luxury and hospitality, and for those seeking a mix of culture and coastal adventure, Tiger Bay is a hub of vibrant markets and charming seaside cafes. Indeed, Lamang is far from the dreary caricature some might imagine. For travelers seeking beauty, tranquility, and authentic Southeast Asian charm, Lamang is not only worth a visit—it’s a must-see. Lamang Celebrates! Farmers across Lamang are rejoicing after an unusually successful rubber harvest this season. Favorable weather conditions and improved tapping techniques contributed to a significant increase in latex yield, with some regions reporting their best results in over a decade. This achievement reflects the strength of Lamang’s agricultural policy and the resilience of its people. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh It’s honestly disheartening to see Western countries label our free and proud nation as a dictatorship. For centuries, they exploited us — and now they preach from some imaginary moral high ground? The West is bombing countries across the globe, yet we’re painted as the villains? Thankfully, not everyone in the West is blind to the double standards their governments push on the world. Just recently, I spoke with a couple of Americans at Hunter’s Paradise — a wonderful place, by the way; you should visit if you get the chance — and they were genuinely ashamed of how Lamang is portrayed back home. I’m truly grateful for people like them. They give me hope that the West can still move beyond its post-colonial mindset. Film Review by Nok Dam — The Running Man Edgar Wright’s The Running Man is a gripping reboot, with a streetwise visual style and emotional core. Glen Powell may not have the raw charisma or acting chops of Arnold Schwarzenegger, but he delivers a solid performance that grounds the story. Wright once again proves his remarkable talent for adaptation — as he did with Scott Pilgrim vs. the World — and this film only reinforces that reputation. It’s just a pity he’s British. 8/10 Fun with Girls My grandfather has the heart of a lion and a lifetime ban from the zoo.

raw.name: Newspaper - Plans For The Future
raw.transcript: Plans For The Future June 26, 1996 Following the sorrowful passing of our liberator and former President, Raksmei Sayavong, his son, Narith Sayavong, has taken on the solemn responsibility of leading our nation into the new millennium. One of his first directives is to strengthen the development of both industry and tourism Across the island, voices of hope and excitement can be heard as new opportunities arise, offering people the chance to learn, grow, and improve their lives. “We want to be more open to the world and create new opportunities for the proud people of Lamang who are striving for a better future. New jobs will be created, and anyone willing can take part and find fulfillment,” said President Narith Sayavong during his inauguration speech. Renaming of Fort Raksmei With the inauguration of our new President, Narith Sayavong, it was officially announced that Fort Raksmei would henceforth bear the name Fort Narith, in his honor. “When I heard the news, I could not hold back my tears of joy. There was no more fitting decision,” said one worker, echoing the sentiments shared by citizens across Lamang. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh When one era comes to an end, another begins. The reign of Raksmei Sayavong was marked by the restoration of our independence and the pursuit of stability during the turbulent Cold War era. Now, under the leadership of Narith Sayavong, Lamang steps forward into a new world order, ready to share our beautiful culture with the world. As someone who once stood among the Sons of Lamang during the great liberation, it is both humbling and inspiring to witness a new generation rise and carry the torch into a brighter future. I hold the deepest confidence that President Narith Sayavong will transform Lamang into a true paradise on Earth. We stand with you, Mr. President. Film Review by Nok Dam — Eraser A middling action flick starring a weary-looking Arnold Schwarzenegger as yet another special agent. Eraser plays like a hollow echo of 80s action movies. The special effects verge on comical, and the so-called high-tech weapons look like props from a paranoid Western fever dream. If you want a Schwarzenegger film where everything actually works, revisit Commando (1985). As for this one? I’d gladly erase Eraser from memory. 6/10 Fun with Girls Why did an old man fall into a well? Because he couldn’t see that well!

raw.name: Newspaper - President Discovers Ancient Vase
raw.transcript: President Discovers Ancient Vase July 1, 2005 While diving in Namlai Lake, President Narith Sayavong made an extraordinary discovery — an ancient, perfectly preserved vase believed to come from a long-forgotten civilization. “I couldn’t believe my luck. It felt as if the vase had been waiting for me,” said the President, visibly moved. “It’s difficult to grasp that I happened upon something so beautiful.” That such a remarkable artifact was uncovered not by scholars or explorers, but by our very own leader, is a moment of great pride for the nation. A symbol of how Lamang continues to connect its rich past with its bright future. Man Steals Chocolate, Forgets Daughter While Fleeing A 40-year-old man attempted to steal a box of chocolates from a convenience store in Pha Lang.
