When confronted by the store owner, he abandoned the chocolates and fled the scene, leaving his young daughter behind in the shop. The child was later safely returned to her mother, while authorities continue their search for the fugitive father. In the end, he left empty-handed in more ways than one. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh Our island is steeped in mystery. There are still places untouched by archaeologists, places that hold secrets from a long-forgotten past. We know for certain that an advanced civilization once inhabited this area, although its name remains unknown. From time to time, when forests are cleared, we uncover fragments of walls or ancient ruins. But to discover a perfectly preserved ancient vase — and by sheer chance — is extraordinary. It feels like a sign. Our President is truly blessed to lead a nation as proud and rich in history as ours. Film Review by Nok Dam — Batman Begins Batman Begins is a fresh start for the famed comic-book hero. Under Christopher Nolan’s direction, the film adopts a more grounded approach, focusing on Bruce Wayne’s origins and the training that would later allow him to fight crime in Gotham City. At its core, the story reflects the failure of the Western system to protect its own citizens, portraying a society so broken that only a wealthy businessman has the resources to restore order. While Christian Bale delivers a solid performance, Michael Keaton’s portrayal of Batman remains far more iconic. Nolan is undeniably a talented filmmaker, but the disparaging fact is that he’s of British origin. 6/10 Fun with Girls What do you call a shoe made out of a banana? A slipper.

raw.name: Newspaper - Raksmei Sayavong (1924-1996)
raw.transcript: Raksmei Sayavong (1924-1996) June 23, 1996 It is with great sorrow that we must announce the death of our beloved leader and the father of our free nation. He tragically lost his life in an automobile accident, and with him, the world has lost a towering figure who helped shape modern history. Let us honor the sacrifices he made in the name of freedom. As a young man, he was obliged to leave his family and join the freedom fighters who stood bravely against a criminal regime that took power after the expulsion of the vicious British. In 1968, his lifelong dream became reality when he led the liberation of the Lamang people. Under his leadership, the Sons of Lamang fulfilled their mission and established a legitimate democratic government. That same year, fortune smiled on him once more with the birth of his son, Narith, who now, with a heavy heart, takes up the mantle to lead our nation into a new millennium. His legacy will be remembered with deep admiration for generations to come. Farewell, beloved liberator. National Mourning From every corner of Lamang, the people's cries and sorrow can be heard throughout the land. Citizens are in disbelief at the immense loss our nation has suffered. Work has come to a standstill as the workers cannot steady their trembling hands, and offices remain closed as tears stream down the faces of those inside. The entire nation mourns the passing of our leader, our hero, our liberator. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh The heart of our great leader, burning with unwavering love for his people, has ceased to beat. This is the greatest tragedy in the nation's history. As I write these words, the emptiness is beyond expression. Our beloved President, Raksmei Sayavong, has left us forever. It feels inconceivable. In the streets, people wail in despair, tearing their clothes in sorrow. Even our strongest soldiers weep openly, unable to contain the grief that grips the nation. What shall we do without our liberator? The man who led the Sons of Lamang to glorious victory over a corrupt regime... who rewrote our destiny and left an indelible mark on the world. Even the heavens weep for the fallen President, the man who brought eternal glory to the Lamangese people. Comment by Nok Dam There can be no film review when the nation is in mourning over the tragic loss of our beloved liberator. Gone is the hero who struck down the corrupt regime that conspired with foreign powers. Gone is the President who loved his people fiercely and dared to stand against the mightiest forces in the world. Gone is the man who changed his destiny, and ours too. We will never forget you, President Raksmei Sayavong. Thank you for everything. Raksmei Sayavong Quote: “Our nation has a responsibility to stand as a shining example of an independent and resilient small country, inspiring others like us to break free from Western imperialist domination. Stand firm, Lamang.”

raw.name: Newspaper - Reds Seize Another Country!
raw.transcript: Reds Seize Another Country! January 20, 1970 The USSR continues its expansion into the developing world, with its latest target being the small Southeast Asian nation of Lamang. After two decades of independence and progress, the country descended into turmoil when a rebel faction known as the Sons of Lamang seized power in 1968 following a brief civil war. Their rise was swift and brutal: political opponents executed, dissent silenced, and democratic institutions dismantled. The faction’s leader, Raksmei Sayavong, has since declared himself President and rebranded the country as the Democratic Republic of Lamang — a title that does little to hide the regime’s authoritarian nature. It is now all but confirmed that the Soviet Union supported this violent takeover from the very beginning. Without Moscow’s backing, the rebels could never have toppled the legitimate government so quickly. That investment is already paying off, as reports of Soviet-funded construction projects on Lamang reach U.S. forces currently aiding the fight for freedom in Vietnam. One can only hope, and pray, that the people of Lamang will one day rise against their oppressors and return to the community of free nations. Viet Cong Hiding in Neighboring Countries Growing concerns point to the Viet Cong and North Vietnamese Army using sanctuaries in Cambodia. Tensions are rising along the border as the conflict shows no signs of slowing. Interview — General Thomas C. Waters Q: General, can you tell us what exactly happened in Lamang? A: During the civil war, the Soviets supplied the Sons of Lamang with weapons and resources. With that support, the rebels quickly overthrew the legitimate government. In return, the new regime has begun openly cooperating with Moscow. Q: Do we know what is being built there? A: Nothing good, that much is clear. We suspect a radar facility, most likely for intelligence-gathering and surveillance aimed at our operations in Vietnam. Q: Will the United States be taking any action? A: If you’re asking whether we intend to invade Lamang, the answer is no. That’s not on the table. Our focus is elsewhere at the moment. But rest assured, we’ll be monitoring them very closely. Q: Thank you for your time, General. A: The pleasure is mine. Letters to the Editor Good day, I must admit, I’ve been losing sleep over the constant reports about the spread of communism. It feels like a threat looming over civilization. Could you focus on a different topic for a while so that I might find some peace of mind? Thank you, Karen B. Dear Karen, You’re right to be afraid of the communist plague; it is a real threat. The Reds are relentless, and they never sleep. That’s why you shouldn’t either! Stay alert, stay ready. And no, we will not stop reporting on them. That’s exactly what they would want!

raw.name: Newspaper - Slavers Shut Down
raw.transcript: Slavers Shut Down December 2, 2024 Police units carried out a successful raid targeting organized crime near the Blue Lagoon earlier this week. The infamous Fanny Paradise strip club was shut down, and its owner was taken into custody after authorities uncovered evidence of human trafficking and forced labor. “We will not stand for these kinds of practices in Lamang,” said Vice President Jan Park. “Let this serve as a clear message: those who exploit others will be brought to justice.” Moments like this remind us of the strength of our institutions. Lamang remains a country committed to safety, justice, and the values of a true democracy. President Narith Sayavong Visits Sunset Chalet President Narith Sayavong, accompanied by Vice President Jan Park, paid a visit to Sunset Chalet near the Midnight Sapphire Resort, where they admired the breathtaking scenery and enjoyed a cup of coffee. “It was truly a life-changing experience to have the honor of serving our great leader, President Narith Sayavong,” said Khempheng Thammavong, a waitress at Sunset Chalet. “I will cherish this memory for the rest of my life. I feel truly blessed.” Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh Our nation is built on cooperation and mutual trust. That’s why it’s always disheartening to hear of individuals who seek to undermine that foundation. What took place in that infamous strip club — whose name I won’t even dignify by mentioning — stands in direct opposition to the values our country upholds. Even in the most tolerant societies, a few rotten apples will emerge. Fortunately, we have the means to prevent disgraceful acts like this from spreading. If you witness anything similar in your community, do not hesitate — report it to the police or government authorities. Let it be known: crime has no place in Lamang. Film Review by Nok Dam — Wicked I was seriously tempted to walk out of the theater, but I managed to hold it together. It's part of the job. On the other hand, you don't need to suffer like I did, so do yourself a favor and skip this soulless mess. Not a single song sticks, not even by accident. More and more, it feels like the West is trying to erode our culture through its entertainment industry. Wicked isn't just bad; it's a weaponized form of boredom, right up there with The Boy and the Heron. 1/10 Fun with Girls Have you heard the joke about yoga? Never mind, it's a bit of a stretch.

raw.name: Newspaper - Suburbs Controversy
raw.transcript: Suburbs Controversy October 20, 2019 Rumors have been circulating about a new real estate development project on the outskirts of the city. Many locals have spoken out, raising concerns about potential harm to the environment and suggesting the development caters exclusively to wealthy individuals looking to isolate themselves from the broader community. We reached out to the mayor for comment. "I want to reassure everyone that the project will comply fully with the law, and that the natural surroundings will be protected," the mayor said. "Claims that these new buildings are only for the upper class are simply untrue. This development will create a wide range of opportunities, including essential services and jobs that will benefit the entire community." As promised, we looked into the issue. With the mayor's statement, concerned residents can feel confident that the project is being handled with care and consideration. We're glad to have brought some clarity to the conversation. Tragedy at Tonmai Hainy Lumber Company A terrible tragedy occurred at the Tonmain Hainy Lumber Company when a falling log struck and killed a worker instantly. In response to circulating rumors, a company spokesperson stated: “We want to reassure the public that our company is not cursed, despite recent speculation. While this marks the third fatal accident in recent years, these incidents are not the result of anything supernatural. Unfortunately, they stem from workers disregarding proper safety procedures.” Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh From time to time, the state must clear parts of our beautiful wilderness to make way for new projects. While this may seem unfortunate, it is a necessary step made with careful thought and purpose. Trust that the government understands what is needed to build a better future. Every such project is backed by extensive planning, analysis, and documentation to ensure it brings lasting value to our nation. What might appear today as the loss of heritage is, in truth, a transformation, an investment in what lies ahead. What belonged to yesterday may no longer serve the needs of tomorrow. So let us not mourn what is passing. Instead, let us look forward with a spirit of progress and renewal, knowing that the benefits of today’s decisions will shape a stronger, brighter future for us all. Film Review by Nok Dam — The Lighthouse Robert Pattinson and Willem Dafoe deliver outstanding performances as lighthouse keepers who are slowly losing their grip on reality. Director Robert Eggers creates a surreal, claustrophobic story filled with myth, psychological dread, and farting. Overall, it's an intriguing exploration of the human psyche and the encounter with the unknown. 8/10 Fun with Girls Why should you never play poker at the zoo? Too many cheetahs.

raw.transcript: Honoring the Best Workers May 2, 2016 A day to remember. Each year, on the eve of Labour Day, comes a tradition that leaves a lasting mark — the honoring of the nation’s finest workers by President Narith Sayavong. Long before the ceremony began, the corridor linking the Representation Room to Parliament was alive with energy. Nominees for honorary titles, state decorations, and national awards gathered with visible excitement and anticipation. “I can’t wait to shake hands with our beloved President. I’ll be telling my grandchildren about this,” said Wai Lor, a construction worker from Chon village, beaming with pride. The Voice of the People Echoed Across the Nation: Our Security Lies in the Party’s Policy! May Day was celebrated across Lamang as a testament to the joyful lives of workers. President Narith Sayavong delivered a stirring and unforgettable speech, reflecting on the nation’s turbulent past while promising a radiant future for every worker. His words resonated deeply, moving citizens to tears in every corner of the country. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh There is no day more meaningful to workers than Labor Day. For the individuals and groups chosen to meet our esteemed President Narith Sayavong, it is truly a life-changing experience. We all know of the President’s extraordinary achievements, but seeing him in person is something entirely different. The heroic figure we read about or hear in speeches becomes real before our very eyes. It feels as though a higher being has stepped down to walk among us. I cannot help but envy those meeting the President for the first time. I would give anything to relive that moment. Film Review by Nok Dam — The Nice Guys The Nice Guys is an entertaining ride from legendary writer-director Shane Black. This detective buddy comedy follows Russell Crowe and Ryan Gosling as they navigate through a chaotic and genuinely engaging mystery. If you’re looking for a fun film that doesn’t try to be more than it is, I wholeheartedly recommend it. 8/10 Fun with Girls I got a new pen that can write underwater. It can write other words too.

raw.name: Newspaper - The Midnight Sapphire Miracle
raw.transcript: The Midnight Sapphire Miracle March 11, 2009 Hundreds of our fellow citizens are volunteering to be evicted from their homes as they understand the imposing vision of our wise President Narith Sayavong. "When I heard that our President has such grand plans for the place where my family and I have lived for generations, I started to cry with pride. It is an honor to make way for such a project," said one of the residents. Construction of the Midnight Sapphire Resort has already begun, creating new jobs for many Lamangese natives. "I am excited that the entire Lamang nation shares my vision for the future of our country," Narith Sayavong commented. "Together, and only together, we will build a paradise on earth." A marvelous statement from our beloved leader. We wish all local citizens the best of luck in finding a new home through the relocation program and look forward to the completion of the magnificent Midnight Sapphire. A Stump Was on Fire in Nam Thaven Shortly before 1 p.m. on Tuesday, firefighters went to the outskirts of Nam Thaven. A stump was on fire, so they extinguished it and returned to the base. Authorities confirm that the situation was handled promptly and there is no threat to the public. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh At times, I feel almost ashamed of how much our beloved state does for us. Have I truly earned these privileges? Have I done enough to deserve the care and support I receive? I know I’m not alone in these thoughts. Many of you must feel the same. Our state nurtures us, gives us purpose, educates us, and guides us through life, like devoted parents who are always there and always dependable. It shocks me to see how the West treats its citizens. A society ruled by brute power, tearing itself apart like a wounded beast. Millions sleep on cold streets while the Western states look away, indifferent in their apathy. It’s horrifying. Here in Lamang, we are truly fortunate. So, instead of asking what more the state can do for us, let’s ask ourselves what we can do for it. Let’s give back the love, care, and stability it has so generously given us. Film Review by Nok Dam — Watchmen Watchmen is a comic book adaptation that explores the personal struggles and deep flaws of its so-called superheroes as they navigate their complicated lives. It is an exceptional adaptation with phenomenal actors. The scenes with Rorschach still give me chills. If you're looking for a movie that dives into tough moral choices and the blurry line between right and wrong, this one’s a must-watch. The biggest downfall of this movie is that the author of the comics, Alan Moore, is British. 9/10 Fun with Girls A horse walks into a bar and the bartender says: "Oh my God! Somebody call animal services!"

raw.name: Newspaper - The Three Hundredth Anniversary
raw.transcript: The Three Hundredth Anniversary October 12, 1993 Like many nations across the globe, we too were “discovered” by the wretched Westerners in the 17th century. We remember with hatred the times when the British and the Japanese occupied our island. But let us never forget, it wasn’t these empires who first stained our sacred soil. No, the first usurpers came from yet another European nation. But I’ll say no more. Let us now hear the words of our liberator, President Raksmei Sayavong: “Three hundred years ago, a Dutch captain named Adriaen Brunel arrived on our shores. He was in charge of a trading ship called the Oosterse Bloem, which sought supplies, food, and fresh water for its crew. We welcomed him. We offered to help, as we have always assisted those in need. And that was our mistake. In the years that followed, the Westerners returned again and again, taking whatever they pleased. Our water, our food, and even our women. This did not stop, including during British rule. We were reduced to slaves. Don't ever forgive the British for what they did to us. But keep a small part of your anger for the Dutch, for it was they who first brought the Western cruelty to our land.” Man Steals Chicken and Locks Himself in a Toilet; Only Bones Were Left A hungry 28-year-old man, without any money, visited Nam Thaven in search of a proper snack. He seized a grilled chicken and locked himself in a toilet, refusing to open the door to authorities until he had finished eating. When the door was finally opened, only the bones remained. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh For much of our recent history, we were nothing more than a British colony, a minuscule dot on their world map. They held us hostage on our own land, working us to the bone. Past events have shown that looking elsewhere brought no comfort. The Dutch had been robbing our resources even before the British arrived. And when our fellow Asians, the Japanese, came, they treated us no better. To them, we were just cheap labor. We once had a strong relationship with the Soviets, but sadly, they too have fallen. And now? Now we watch the world with caution, sensing that the age of new empires is upon us. There is only one nation we can genuinely trust, and that is ourselves: the Lamangese.", Film Review by Nok Dam — Demolition Man Demolition Man offers a dystopian glimpse into a future where Western liberalism has spiraled into absurdity. Beneath the false promises of peace and order, citizens have had their freedoms systematically stripped away. Sylvester Stallone stars as the rugged enforcer of the past, facing off against a hyper-violent Wesley Snipes. Both deliver standout performances. The film is a brilliant, entertaining look at the fate that may await the imperialist world. Director Marco Brambilla shows immense talent, and I’m genuinely excited to see what he does next. 9/10 Fun with Girls What did the janitor say when he jumped out of the closet? Supplies!",

raw.name: Newspaper - The UN Is Allowing Lies to Spread
raw.transcript: The UN Is Allowing Lies to Spread March 23, 2024 It is with deep regret that we must report yet another instance of the United Nations giving a platform to traitorous individuals who fled our homeland only to slander it before the international community. “It’s truly disheartening to hear such lies from our own people,” said Vice President Jan Park. “They claim we are a dictatorship, that we commit atrocities and oppress our citizens. It’s unbelievable. I don’t understand what drives them to speak such harmful untruths, but I sincerely hope they reflect on the damage they’ve done to our country’s reputation and find the courage to apologize. We’ve spoken with some of their family members, and I can assure you they reject these liars.” We wholeheartedly agree. Every nation can strive to improve, and if someone feels wronged, there are proper ways to seek dialogue. But turning to the United Nations to spread malicious falsehoods is not one of them. Tourism Success Positive reports are arriving from across Lamang, marking a highly successful tourist season. “We’re pleased to confirm that the Midnight Sapphire Hotel is fully booked for the coming months,” stated CEO Thongloun Noy. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh A smear campaign against our nation is gaining traction in the West. Those governments simply cannot grasp the reality that we have built a truly self-sufficient paradise. It is disheartening to see some Lamangese abandon such a beautiful homeland to settle in morally decaying foreign lands. Worse still, some of them spread falsehoods about us abroad. Are they being coerced? It is difficult to imagine any other reason why someone would backstab their own country in this way. Thankfully, the growing number of tourists visiting Lamang can see the truth for themselves: our country is among the safest and most stunning places on Earth. Ultimately, it is the ordinary people of the world whose judgment truly matters. And they are the ones who will preserve our nation’s rightful reputation. Film Review by Nok Dam — Dune: Part Two Dune: Part Two is the long-awaited continuation of Denis Villeneuve’s ambitious adaptation of Frank Herbert’s sci-fi masterpiece. Like its predecessor, this installment delivers stunning visual effects, with several scenes that will stay etched in your memory long after the credits roll. However, the pacing stumbles in the middle, only to rush through a finale that feels surprisingly abrupt and lacking in emotional payoff. Despite these flaws, I still wholeheartedly recommend seeing Dune: Part Two on the big screen. It’s an audiovisual experience best enjoyed in full cinematic scale. 8/10 Fun with Girls I couldn't figure out why the baseball kept getting larger. Then it hit me.

raw.name: Newspaper - The World is Watching
raw.transcript: THE WORLD IS WATCHING January 15, 2025 The brilliant vision of our glorious President Narith has put our island on the world map! His grand plans are coming to fruition as foreign newspapers discuss the beautiful Midnight Sapphire Resort. But enough of my writing; here is the praise from the Worldview News. "The number one tourist destination for wealthy individuals has become the Midnight Sapphire Resort in the Democratic Republic of Lamang. This small country in Southeast Asia is making big waves lately as many Hollywood stars praise the generosity of the locals and the modern approach to hospitality service they have experienced." It's wonderful to read such warm words from our foreign colleagues. We are sure there will be more similar articles about our beautiful homeland to share with our dear readers. Scientific Breakthrough in National Productivity Recent findings from our nation's top scientists have uncovered a remarkable, some might even say sacred, phenomenon. Every time our esteemed President, Narith Sayavong, visits a workplace, there is a statistically significant boost in productivity. "This is indeed the case," confirmed Professor Phai Lor. "We've dubbed it the Sayavong Effect, and we're currently exploring methods to harness this phenomenon on a national scale." Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh Our land is a paradise. You might have your doubts; maybe you've seen a glossy Hollywood film or some polished foreign promo, but believe me, there's no place like Lamang. I've traveled the world. I've seen the skyscrapers of New York, wandered through Russia, sipped coffee beneath the Eiffel Tower, eaten sushi in Okinawa, and even braved the dreariness of London… But none of those places come close to the richness of our culture. There's something truly special here, something you only begin to understand once you leave. And that's precisely why I urge you: don't go! Don't waste your time. Out there, it's a barren land. There's a reason so many Lamangese return after chasing illusions abroad. And above all, we have universal healthcare! That alone speaks volumes. Film Review by Nok Dam — Kadhalikka Neramillai Kadhalikka Neramillai is a charming Indian romantic comedy written and directed by Kiruthiga Udhayanidhi. The film explores themes of modern relationships, single parenthood, and societal expectations, with a focus on how differing views on family and relationships evolve. Even though the second part is a little weaker, the film still feels like a breath of fresh air compared to many formulaic Hollywood rom-coms. Definitely give it a chance. It’s entertaining and, in many ways, relatable. After all, like us, Indians have also endured the cruelty of the British Empire. In spirit, they’re like cousins. 7/10 Fun with Girls Never confide in a vacuum cleaner. They’re always collecting dirt.

raw.name: Newspaper - There's no Reason to Panic
raw.transcript: There's no reason to panic November 26, 2025 "Undoubtedly, an unwarranted panic is spreading throughout our society. Lies and delusions have infected the minds of our fellow citizens and are eating away at the community we have so long built together. Do not be fooled by rumors that have no basis in reality. Our country has never been better." These are the words of Vice President Jan Park, and we have to agree. As journalists with a duty to present truthful information and news to our fellow citizens, we are compelled to make a similar statement to our readers. There is no indication that anything unusual is happening. We are one of the safest countries in the world, and no one will divide our community. Obey All Orders from the Armed Forces There have been recent incidents where civilians failed to comply with instructions from police and military personnel. We remind all citizens that order must be maintained, especially during these exceptional circumstances. Respect the law. Cooperate fully. This situation is temporary, and with unity and discipline, normal life will resume soon. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh My fellow citizens — can’t you see what’s happening right before your eyes? Isn’t it obvious that everything we’ve witnessed is part of a psychological war waged by foreign intelligence agencies? They’ve tried everything: lies, slander, persecution. But they haven’t broken us. We are strong. We are united. Do not let the colonizers — those parasites — tear apart our beautiful homeland. They want us gone. They send their lackeys, the so-called United Nations Lamang Relief Agency, to do their dirty work. And when your homes are abandoned, they’ll move in and call upon their armies to claim whatever is left. Make no mistake: the West is eager to colonize us once again. DO NOT BELIEVE THEIR LIES! Film Review by Nok Dam — Wicked: For Good This film is as dreadful as the situation Lamang now faces under the weight of Western oppression. The first installment was already a slog — forgettable songs and shallow, millennial-grade writing — and the sequel offers nothing but more of the same. Curse the creators of this mess. I was forced to sit through it during one of the darkest chapters in our island’s history. 1/10 Fun with Girls Why did the scarecrow win an award? Because he was outstanding in his field.

raw.name: Newspaper - Trial of the Nation's Traitors
raw.transcript: Trial of the Nation's Traitors December 5, 1968 Yesterday, twelve former government officials were found guilty of high treason and sentenced to death by hanging. These individuals, who had clearly served British imperialist interests over those of our own people, faced the full weight of justice. The people of Lamang are angry and disgusted by their crimes. The State Prosecutor's Office has received hundreds of resolutions, including those from factories and offices. "We demand the strictest possible punishment for the troublemakers," write the lumberjacks and other workers of the old timber factories. Other resolutions, equally angry, but reflecting the firm belief of our people in maintaining lasting peace, are addressed to those who have broken all international laws most shamefully and have launched a campaign against our young democracy. "In the name of the people of Lamang, let the sentence fall like an iron fist — without an ounce of mercy!" declared the presiding judge in a powerful closing statement. He emphasized that in the new democratic country, those who betray their homeland will face swift and uncompromising punishment. The citizens of Lamang welcomed the verdict with overwhelming approval. We will not allow the Republic to fall apart! Long live democracy! General Joy With revolutionary fervor, songs of joy and celebration echo across Lamang. “Long live the Republic! Long live our beloved President Raksmei Sayavong!” cry the peasants and workers in unison. The dark shadows of ourcolonial legacy have been cast away. At last, the citizens of Lamang can breathe freely in the light of true independence! Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh I was born in the jungle. My earliest memory is of my family fleeing from the ruthless forces of the traitors who seized our homeland and violated it. I curse them. Because of them, I never had a childhood. From the very beginning, I was a warrior… and a dreamer. I studied grand political theories from a young age — not for leisure, but out of necessity. I had to defend my ideals and spread the truth among the oppressed people of Lamang. The old regime fostered ignorance and illiteracy, yet had the audacity to call us barbarians. While my peers toiled in rice paddies to feed pompous officials in their villas, I devoured the works of Marx, Nietzsche, and Sartre by the age of seven. But now, a new chapter begins. It's time to purge the rot — those who tried to keep us buried in the mud. We will destroy them as we destroy illiteracy, poverty, and nepotism. This is the dawn of a new age, an age of opportunity for every citizen of Lamang. You needn't look far for proof. Look at me. When before was it ever possible for a jungle-born, despised by the old world, to become a journalist… at just fifteen? Film Review by Nok Kao — Planet of the Apes Planet of the Apes is a revolutionary movie that blends science fiction themes with sharp social commentary. The story is about a cosmonaut stranded in a world ruled by intelligent apes, where humans have been reduced to primitive creatures. I won't say more to avoid spoiling the brilliant story and its unexpected ending. The makeup effects are gorgeous, and the script is rich with thought-provoking ideas. If you get the chance to visit the cinema, don't hesitate. 9/10 Lonely Hearts Businessman, single, handsome Fifty-five years old, tall, and wealthy. Due to a lack of time and opportunity, seeks a sympathetic, pretty girl or a lady with some dowry. Recommendations from parents, relatives, or acquaintances are welcome. Mark: Discretion guaranteed.

raw.name: Newspaper - UN Concludes Lamang Evacuation
raw.transcript: UN Concludes Lamang Evacuation December 2, 2025 The United Nations Lamang Relief Agency (UNLRA) has announced the successful completion of its evacuation operation in the Southeast Asian nation of Lamang. "We are pleased to confirm that the entire population of Lamang Island has been evacuated," the statement read. "We extend our gratitude to all nations that accepted refugees and assisted in this logistically demanding mission." The evacuation took place between November 24 and December 1, following a massive explosion of unknown origin around 11:00 PM on November 24. UN Imposes Quarantine In the wake of the evacuation, the United Nations has declared an international quarantine on the island of Lamang. All entry is strictly prohibited until further notice. Interview — Patricia Bell, Ph.D. Q: Dr. Bell, as an expert on Southeast Asia, could you explain what happened in Lamang? A: After the explosion that shook the island, the UNLRA organized a mass evacuation. While the operation is being presented as smooth and successful, the reality is likely more complicated. Certain details about the evacuation and the events leading up to it are almost certainly classified or deliberately withheld. It will take time before the full picture emerges. Q: Are there any indications as to why the UN has placed the island under quarantine? A: The quarantine is almost certainly linked to the explosion. Whether it was chemical, biological, or even nuclear in nature is still speculation. What is clear is that not everyone will honor the quarantine. Even now, some groups are likely finding ways to infiltrate the island for looting or other purposes. And we know with certainty that dictator Narith Sayavong did not evacuate. Q: Do you believe this could signal a new kind of conflict in Southeast Asia? A: It’s possible, though the motives remain unclear. Lamang, despite being a dictatorship, was highly insular and showed no expansionist ambitions. If it was attacked, the culprit was likely not a nation-state but a non-state actor that somehow acquired a weapon of mass destruction. Q: Thank you for your insights, Dr. Bell. A: You’re welcome. Letters to the Editor Why won’t you write the truth??? It’s all over the internet!!! The ALIENS visited Lamang!!!!!!!!!!!! TELL THE TRUTH!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Chungus B. Dear Chungus, It’s somewhat ironic that you demand the truth yet won’t even sign your message with your real name. If we had undeniable evidence that aliens were responsible for what happened in Lamang, we would report it without hesitation. Unfortunately, no such evidence exists at this time; all available information points to elsewhere.

raw.name: Newspaper - United Nations Mission
raw.transcript: United Nations Mission July 13, 2025 Today, the United Nations arrived in our homeland. To avoid any confusion, we are publishing the official statement from President Narith Sayavong regarding the UN’s decision to launch an operation in Lamang: “Many of you may be afraid, thinking the UN has invaded our homeland — but rest assured, they are here with my full approval. For too long, our nation has been slandered on the world stage as a so-called dictatorship that oppresses its people. I know that’s not true. You know that’s not true. And now, the whole world will see the truth for itself. If anyone feels their voice has not been heard, you are welcome to speak with UN representatives — known here as the UNLRA. But let me make one thing clear: I am always here to listen. No one else will help us — only Lamangese people can truly help one another.” We are proud to publish this statement from our President and urge all citizens to remain calm during the arrival of the UNLRA. The United Nations will soon see for themselves that the accusations against us were false — and that we have nothing to hide. Lowest Crime Rate The Democratic Republic of Lamang is experiencing a sixth consecutive year of plummeting crime statistics. “We are doing a good job educating the people that crime does not pay,” police spokesman Sao Yang commented. Commentary by Khamphanh Vongphachanh We have always upheld transparency in our nation. There are no hidden truths to uncover. That is precisely why we allowed the presence of UN forces. Their mission is to witness firsthand that Lamang is a peaceful and modern democracy.
